newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN HAINAUT TO GET NO MORE EU MANNA AFTER 2000.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN HAINAUT TO GET NO MORE EU MANNA AFTER 2000.

text.p: The European Union's plan to take on new members without boosting financial resources will lead to the exclusion of Belgian region Hainaut from the most generous European aid schemes from 2000, EU sources said.
"Hainaut will no longer be part of the Objective 1 structural funds for help to the EU's poorest regions," a European Commission official told Reuters on Friday.
Hainaut, British Merseyside and Dutch Flevoland joined this category of regions, which absorb two thirds of the 33 billion Ecus budget for structural development funds, in 1994.
The three regions had been allowed in, despite the fact that their GDP was greater than 75 percent of the EU average, which is normally the threshold.
A financing plan for enlargement towards the East, which the Commission plans to present on Wednesday, proposes keeping financial means unchanged between 2000 and 2006.
To achieve this, the Commission will also propose tightening the criteria for benefitting from Objective 1 funds, meaning Hainaut is set to lose its preferential treatment.
